name: Scene and prop model
observations: OpenMontage’s primary Explainer model is a time-addressed array of cuts: each cut has id, source, in_seconds, and out_seconds, with optional type-specific fields; ExplainerProps requires cuts and optionally accepts overlays, captions, and audio. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:187-308.

The Cut shape is an extensible prop bag rather than a closed discriminated union: it includes text/stat/card/comparison/chart/progress fields, media/background fields, animation and transform fields, anime-scene fields, terminal-scene fields, and screenshot-scene fields. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:187-268.

SceneRenderer dispatches first on explicit cut.type and required props, then on source filename extension for image/video media, then falls back to treating any source as an image, and finally renders a text card using cut.text or cut.id when no source/type is usable. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:555-772.

Each cut is rendered in a Remotion Sequence whose frame start is round(in_seconds*fps) and duration is round((out_seconds-in_seconds)*fps); overlays use the same time conversion. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:834-870.

Background media is orthogonal to the scene component: backgroundVideo takes precedence over backgroundImage, both receive an overlay opacity default of 0.55, and the selected component is rendered above the layer. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:480-579.

Explainer has four effective visual/data layers: animated theme background, visual scenes, overlays, and captions; audio is added as narration and music tracks. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:841-917.

The separate cinematic model is a closed union of video and title scenes. Both share id/startSeconds/durationSeconds; video adds src, tone, trims, playbackRate, filter, and fade frames, while title adds text/accent/intensity/background trim fields/variant. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:1-32.

CinematicRendererProps carries scenes plus title sizing, signal-line count, soundtrack/music, and caption configuration; soundtrack and music are both accepted as compatibility-shaped fields. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:34-67.

Root registers independent Remotion compositions for Explainer and CinematicRenderer, with 1920x1080 at 30fps defaults. Explainer metadata uses the greatest cut out_seconds plus one second of padding, or 30 seconds when cuts are empty. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Root.tsx:123-151 and 153-176.

Demo props show the cut model being used as declarative scene data: empty source plus explicit component types, per-cut time windows, text/chart/stat fields, and separate overlays. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/public/demo-props/code-to-screen.json:1-93, focusflow-pitch.json:1-93, world-in-numbers.json:1-95.

The demo catalog documents chart, card, anime, terminal, screenshot, and overlay/provider-chip types and identifies required/common fields, making the catalog an operational part of the model’s discoverability. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/SCENE_TYPES.md:9-38.
OpenMontage’s repository declares AGPL licensing in /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/LICENSE; this analysis treats it as an observation target, not as permission to reuse implementation or assets.
inferences: The effective OpenMontage scene model is a layered timeline IR: cuts define timed visual units, overlays are independently timed annotations, and backgrounds are compositional wrappers rather than separate timeline entities.

The model favors permissive forward evolution over compile-time exhaustiveness: adding a scene type requires extending the Cut interface, adding a renderer dispatch branch, exporting the component, and documenting it, but unknown data is not rejected by the runtime dispatch path.

The explicit type plus required-field checks provide soft validation through dispatch rather than a formal schema validator; malformed or incomplete typed cuts can silently reach later fallbacks or render blank/partial component content.

The model supports both asset-backed scenes and asset-free synthetic scenes. Demo props demonstrate that a prop object can be entirely declarative and source-free when a component type supplies the visual implementation.

The cinematic union is intentionally narrower and more stable than the general Explainer cut bag, suggesting two compatibility tiers: a broad explainer composition for many component types and a focused cinematic composition for video/title sequencing.

MPS’s current storyboard is a pedagogical planning IR, while OpenMontage’s cuts are a render-oriented timeline IR; direct field-for-field substitution would lose timing semantics, component selection, overlays, and media/background behavior.
OpenMontage’s frame conversion and metadata padding imply that boundary rounding and final-fade padding are observable playback contracts, not merely implementation details.
unknowns: No formal JSON Schema or runtime validation for Explainer cuts, overlays, or demo props was found in the inspected scope; the exact accepted numeric ranges, overlap policy, and behavior for negative or zero durations remain unspecified.

The inspected scene/prop scope does not establish whether overlapping cuts are intentional, how z-order is controlled among cuts, or whether array order is the only ordering rule; Sequence mount order suggests array order may matter, but this should not be treated as proven without renderer tests.

The scope does not identify a canonical schema for chartData, chartSeries, progressSegments, TerminalStep, ScreenshotStep, ParticleType, or WordCaption; several are imported or declared elsewhere and require separate analysis if MPS needs those types.
The exact behavior of missing assets, invalid image/video extensions, failed media decoding, and out-of-range backgroundOverlay values is not specified by the inspected model files.
The relationship between soundtrack and music in CinematicRendererProps is ambiguous from the type alone; whether one aliases the other or has precedence is outside the requested types file.
OpenMontage tests/scripts specific to these scene props were not located in the inspected path listing; therefore demo JSON demonstrates shape and intent but not exhaustive behavioral guarantees.
MPS currently has no first-class prop/entity model corresponding to OpenMontage’s reusable component props, background wrappers, or synthetic UI step primitives.
contracts: A valid Explainer request supplies cuts; each usable cut should have an id and a positive interval represented by in_seconds/out_seconds, with rendering scheduled at 30fps in the default composition.
A cut with a recognized type is eligible for that component only when its required discriminating fields are present; otherwise the renderer may continue to another branch or fallback.

For media fallback, image extensions are recognized from a fixed image-extension list and video extensions from a fixed video-extension list; unknown sources are attempted as images before the final text-card fallback. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:314-325 and 744-772.

backgroundVideo takes precedence over backgroundImage when both are present; both are rendered behind the scene with a configurable/default dark overlay. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:555-579.

Explainer duration metadata is the maximum cut end plus one second, converted with ceil at 30fps; empty cuts default to 30 seconds. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Root.tsx:123-132.

Cinematic scenes must conform to the discriminated kinds video or title and share stable timeline identity/timing fields. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/cinematic/types.ts:3-32.

Overlay timing is independent of cut timing and overlays are rendered after visual scenes, so overlays can span or bridge scene boundaries. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:858-870.

Demo prop files are JSON-serializable declarative inputs and use empty source strings for synthetic typed scenes; consumers must not assume every scene has an external media asset. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/openmontage-analysis/remotion-composer/public/demo-props/code-to-screen.json:3-13 and 15-70.

For MPS, a scene representation should preserve pedagogical narration, visual goal, equations/assets, validation checks, total duration, and mastery check rather than treating render props as the source of truth. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/video_explainer.py:33-60 and 206-227.
mps_gaps: MPS has only a compact Scene dataclass with id, integer duration, narration, visual_goal, equations, assets, and validation_checks; it lacks OpenMontage-style absolute start/end timing, typed scene discriminants, and per-scene render props. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/video_explainer.py:33-42.

MPS storyboard construction chooses a fixed scene count by style and distributes integer seconds; it does not represent arbitrary overlapping intervals, independent overlay timelines, or frame-level timing. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/video_explainer.py:96-97 and 139-190.

MPS local rendering reduces all scenes to a scene-index selection over global progress and uses one rolling-specific or generic visual primitive; it does not dispatch per-scene component types or render reusable prop-driven cards/charts/UI scenes. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:143-180.

MPS has no equivalent to OpenMontage’s separate overlays, captions-as-timed-word-data, or background image/video wrapper semantics in the storyboard Scene model. Audio exists only as a renderer result boolean in the current RenderResult, not as scene input configuration. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:35-55 and /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:214-225.

MPS visual assets are opaque string lists attached to selected scenes; unlike OpenMontage, there is no typed asset role, transform, animation, camera, background, color, or component-specific prop contract. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/video_explainer.py:38-41 and 145-190.

MPS validation checks that scenes have positive integer durations, narration, visual goals, total duration, and mastery metadata, but does not validate renderability of assets, component props, timeline overlaps, or media timing. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/video_explainer.py:206-227.

MPS’s current output contract is provider/artifact/manifest-oriented and can fall back to SVG scene cards; it does not expose a stable scene IR that a Remotion-like renderer could consume directly. Evidence: /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:216-250 and /home/ubuntu/MPS-git/scripts/production_manifest.py:29-73.
clean_room_recommendations: Define an independently named MPS render IR that keeps the existing pedagogical Storyboard as the source of truth and adds optional render fields such as start_seconds, end_seconds, visual_kind, media_ref, props, overlays, and background. Do not reproduce OpenMontage field names wholesale; document translations from pedagogy to rendering.

Use a closed discriminated union for the first supported MPS visual kinds— for example media, text, equation, diagram, metric, and comparison—plus an explicitly versioned extensible props object. Reject unknown kinds and missing required fields during planning rather than relying on renderer fallbacks.

Preserve integer-second storyboard behavior for compatibility, but derive canonical frame timing in one place with an explicit fps and rounding policy; add tests for adjacent scenes, overlaps, zero/negative durations, and final-duration padding.

Represent overlays and captions as separate timed arrays in the MPS IR, while retaining mastery_check and validation_checks outside render-only props so visual rendering cannot accidentally become a mastery decision.

Introduce typed asset roles and deterministic fallback semantics: distinguish background, foreground, equation, diagram, and reference media; report missing or undecodable assets as structured render warnings/errors instead of silently treating them as images.

Add a reusable prop contract for educational objects—labels, quantities, units, vectors, equations, and motion parameters—so the physics-first renderer can draw stable visuals without coupling pedagogy to Pillow or a particular hosted provider.

Keep provider-specific execution behind the existing render_hybrid boundary and serialize the new scene IR into the storyboard/manifest. This preserves current job idempotency, fallback reporting, and artifact paths while allowing a future Remotion adapter.

Add contract tests modeled on the observed behavior but written independently: typed-scene dispatch, required-prop validation, background precedence, overlay timing, metadata duration calculation, deterministic serialization, and explicit distinction between genuine video artifacts and static fallback assets.

Treat OpenMontage’s AGPL-3.0 implementation and assets as reference-only for clean-room analysis. Reimplement behavior from the contracts above using new names, new structure, and MPS-specific pedagogy/render requirements; do not copy source, assets, or implementation text.
